questions.stem: A 45 year old female patient had STEMI and was treated for the same. She was put on Atorvastatin, dual Antiplatelet therapy, GTN during the attack, and a beta blocker on discharge. Which of the following beta blocker should not be prescribed for the above patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pindolol
  • In patients with Ischemic heart disease, we need to avoid beta-blockers with intrinsic Sympathomimetic properties, because they will partially stimulate Beta 1 and increase the workload on the Heart
  • So in the option pindolol is a beta blocker with intrinsic Sympathomimetic property
  • Avoid beta-blockers with intrinsic Sympathomimetic properties in migraine and IHD Patients.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 211

questions.stem: A patient had a heart rate of 60 bpm and has a family history of bradycardia. She was diagnosed with hypertension. She decided to start with a beta-blocker. Which one is preferred:
questions.solutionHtml:
Pindolol
  • In a patient with bradycardia, it is better to start with a drug with partial agonistic activity like pindolol. they will not further decrease heart rate as they have intrinsic sympathomimetic property
  • If beta blockers like propranolol, carvedilol, or Sotalol are used they further decrease HR
  • So in this case pindolol is preferred


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 211

questions.stem: A β-blocker was prescribed for hypertension in a female asthma patient. After about a week of treatment, the asthma attacks got worse, and the patient was asked to stop taking the β-blocker. Which of the following β-blockers would you suggest as an alternative in this patient that is less likely to worsen her asthma?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metoprolol

Advantages of cardioselective Beta-blockers

  • Don’t cause bronchoconstriction, so can be used in asthma and COPD patients
  • Minimal beta 2 blockade in blood vessels, so can be used in peripheral vascular disease
  • Doesn’t interfere with glucose and fat metabolism, so safe to be used in diabetic and dyslipidemic patients
  • Do not interfere with the exciting capacity of patients

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the graphs given?

options.label: A
options.text: Drug in Graph A is epinephrine

options.label: B
options.text: The effect on HR in graph A can be overcome by anti-muscarinic

options.label: C
options.text: Drug acting in graph C is nor- epinephrine

options.label: D
options.text: Drug acting on graph B is isoproterenol

questions.answerText: The effect on HR in graph A can be overcome by anti-muscarinic
questions.solutionHtml:
The effect on HR in graph A can be overcome by anti-muscarinic

NA

  • acts on α1 + α2 + β1 + β3 but no β2 action
  • acts on the β1 receptor and causes vasoconstriction (α 1 action), so it increases SBP, DBP, and MAP
  • increases peripheral resistance due to vasoconstriction (α 1 action)
  • when given IV it reduces heart rate due to reflex bradycardia by vagal stimulation and this can be overcome by anti-vagal(anti-cholinergic) drugs like atropine

Adrenaline

  • acts on α1 + α2 + β1 + β2 with mild action on β3.
  • causes a rise in systolic but a fall in diastolic BP
  • peripheral resistance decreases because vascular β2 receptors are more sensitive than α receptors
  • MAP increases and it increases heart rate due to β1 action

Isoprenaline

  • Isoprenaline causes a rise in systolic BP (β1—cardiac stimulation)
  • acts on β1 + β2 + β3 but has no α action
  • fall in diastolic BP (β2— vasodilatation)
  • MAP falls
  • Increases heart rate due to β1 Stimulation


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 143

questions.stemHtml: An unknown drug is tested in an experimental setup. The results are given in the table. From the above effects seen, the new drug is likely to be:
questions.solutionHtml:
Beta 1 agonist & beta 2 agonist
  • From the table, we can say that in comparison to the placebo, the new drug has increased heart rate, increased systolic BP, decreased Diastolic BP, and increased cardiac output
  • Beta 1 agonism causes Increased HR, CO, and SBP
  • beta 2 agonism caused vasodilation and causes a decrease in DBP
  • So, the correct answer is Beta 1 agonist & beta 2 agonist


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 139

Dobutamine
  • Dobutamine is a cardiac stimulant, which is beta 1 adrenergic receptors.
  • Not a D1 or D2 receptor agonist as Dopamine.
  • It increases the force of cardiac contraction and output, without significant change in heart rate, peripheral resistance, and BP. As such it has been considered to be a relatively selective beta 1 agonist.
  • Terbutaline, Albuterol (like salbutamol) are Beta 2 agonist
  • Mirabegron is a beta 3 agonist used in overactive bladder

questions.stem: The following beta blockers are contraindicated in renal failure:
questions.solutionHtml:
Propranolol
  • Atenolol, Nadolol, and Sotalol are not metabolized in the liver, are long-acting, and excreted via the kidneys, so contraindicated in renal disease
  • Propranolol is well absorbed after oral administration but has low bioavailability due to high first-pass metabolism in the liver
  • Metabolism of propranolol is dependent on hepatic blood flow


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 162
